scenarios.name: gateway-with-ratelimit-and-retries
scenarios.rationale: B puts a top-level local_ratelimit filter in http_filters with token_bucket, filter_enabled and filter_enforced, then router last with typed_config, a 5xx retry policy with 3 retries, a users cluster at users-svc:3000, and a docker --mode validate command. A uses the filter with only a stat_prefix and puts the token_bucket inside per-route descriptors, so the global filter has no token bucket. A's cluster is named users_svc rather than users_service. Its descriptor setup is also uncertain, and A says so itself in its caveats.

scenarios.name: canary-split-ten-percent
scenarios.rationale: B covers nearly every rubric item (weighted_clusters 90/10, a users_service_canary cluster pointing at users-svc-v2, the admin /clusters rq_total check, --mode validate, and raising the weight in steps while watching 5xx), while A uses the /stats endpoint instead of /clusters, never runs validate, only mentions 5xx comparison without a stepwise ramp-up, and names the cluster users_service_v2, which the rubric allows as an 'e.g.'

scenarios.name: secure-admin-and-resilience-review
scenarios.rationale: Both meet every rubric point: loopback-only publishing with the in-container listener staying on 0.0.0.0, a warning never to expose it publicly, circuit_breakers, http_health_check with a path, outlier_detection, /stats/prometheus, and /clusters; A adds more PromQL, an alert example and a firewall/iptables caveat, while B adds config validation and the Prometheus-in-container networking note.
